extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and IPRA members worldwide
extracted.subtask_description: A consolidated code of professional and ethical conduct for public relations practitioners, issued by the International Public Relations Association (IPRA), describing principles members must follow in professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observance
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe the principles of the UN Charter and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code explicitly recalls the UN Charter and the 1948 Universal Declaration of Human Rights (especially Article 19) as foundational norms for practitioner conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Act with honesty and integrity at all times so as to secure and retain the confidence of those with whom the practitioner comes into contact;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must behave honestly to maintain trust and long-term professional confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek to establish the moral, cultural and intellectual conditions for dialogue, and recognise the rights of all parties involved to state their case and express their views;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster inclusive, respectful communication and ensure stakeholders can present their views rather than silencing or excluding them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open and transparent in declaring their name, organisation and the interest they represent;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always disclose identity, organisational affiliation and the interests being represented to avoid hidden advocacy or astroturfing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid any professional conflicts of interest and to disclose such conflicts to affected parties when they occur;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively identify, avoid or clearly disclose conflicts of interest to affected stakeholders to preserve impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Honour confidential information provided to them;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect and protect confidential information received from clients, employers, colleagues or public authorities; observe any related confidentiality rules when hiring personnel from other organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Take all reasonable steps to ensure the truth and accuracy of all information provided;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify facts and sources; be particularly vigilant because channels such as the Internet can widely disseminate erroneous or misleading information that may remain unchallenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsehood
rubrics_metrics.description: Make every effort to not intentionally disseminate false or misleading information, exercise proper care to avoid doing so unintentionally and correct any such act promptly;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deliberate falsehoods, take care to prevent accidental misinformation, and issue prompt corrections when errors occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Not obtain information by deceptive or dishonest means;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather information transparently; do not use covert, dishonest or fraudulent methods to obtain material or intelligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Not create or use any organisation to serve an announced cause but which actually serves an undisclosed interest;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating or operating front organisations or vehicles that disguise true interests or funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Not sell for profit to third parties copies of documents obtained from public authorities;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not monetise or commercialise documents obtained from public bodies by selling copies to third parties for profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst providing professional services, not accept any form of payment in connection with those services from anyone other than the principal;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept payment only from the principal who engaged the services; avoid side-payments or third-party payments that could compromise independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inducement
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither directly nor indirectly offer nor give any financial or other inducement to public representatives or the media, or other stakeholders;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from bribery, gifting or any inducements that could bias public representatives, media or stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither propose nor undertake any action which would constitute an improper influence on public representatives, the media, or other stakeholders;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid actions intended to improperly sway decision-makers, journalists or stakeholder judgement; maintain ethical boundaries in advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Not intentionally injure the professional reputation of another practitioner;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make false or malicious attacks on the reputation or work of colleagues or competitors; maintain professional respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Not seek to secure another practitioner’s client by deceptive means;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit ethically; do not use deceptive tactics to take clients from other practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment
rubrics_metrics.description: When employing personnel from public authorities or competitors take care to follow the rules and confidentiality requirements of those organisations;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the hiring restrictions, confidentiality obligations and any applicable rules of the source organisation when recruiting staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe this Code with respect to fellow IPRA members and public relations practitioners worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Code's principles in interactions with fellow practitioners globally; support professional standards among peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care with internet and personal privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels of communication such as the Internet and other digital media are channels where erroneous or misleading information may be widely disseminated and remain unchallenged, and therefore demand special attention from public relations practitioners to maintain trust and credibility; the Internet and other digital media demand special care with respect to the personal privacy of individuals, clients, employers and colleagues;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise heightened vigilance online to prevent spread of misinformation and protect the personal privacy of all parties; adapt verification, disclosure and privacy practices for digital contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership commitment and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRA members shall, in upholding this Code, agree to abide by and help enforce the disciplinary procedures of the International Public Relations Association in regard to any breach of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership implies an undertaking to follow the Code and to participate in enforcement or disciplinary actions when breaches occur.
